Technical_Enrichment: Baseline terroir isolate used for comparison against Colombia El Obraje.
Strict adherence to 1:17 brew ratio for all filter coffees to maximize clarity. Minimalist 'no-frills' standing-room-only roastery.

Sensory_Verdict: Simultaneous citric-malic acid overlap with integrated cane sugar — smooth and refreshing with excellent mid-palate juiciness. Confirmed: I love this bean.
Technical_Enrichment: EK43S 98mm flat burrs + V60 conical at 1:16 delivered perfect dual-acid integration (citric orange + malic plum) without single-note dominance. Sucrose extraction at 1:16 bridged the acid structure into clean cane sugar finish.

Target_Notes: Floral aroma; stewed strawberries; grapefruit; brown sugar; black tea aftertaste
Sensory_Verdict: Floral taste with a sweet coating on the tongue that gradually sticks and fades off cleanly like sugar and tea aftertaste.
Technical_Enrichment: Multi-temperature pour (80°C -> 95°C -> 80°C) with Hario Alpha flat-bottom dripper perfectly managed the heavy honey process sugars, allowing clear floral extraction at lower temps and dissolving heavy jammy mucilage at peak heat, finishing cleanly.

Sensory_Verdict: Pretty good. Kiwi and oolong tea style, full bodied. Short finish with slight hints of chocolate.
Technical_Enrichment: Typica's inherent lipid clarity and raised-bed drying produced clean tea-structure body; EK43 + Hario Switch immersion phase stabilised full mouthfeel at 1:17. Short finish consistent with 15-days-off-roast volatile taper.

Sensory_Verdict: Felt hibiscus hot. Mid temp showed apple paste. Cooled to a honeyed character. Full bodied. Textbook style flavors, definitely a good one.
Technical_Enrichment: 90°C brew temp suppressed lactic ester over-extraction while preserving volatile anthocyanin hibiscus esters. Laurina's low caffeine allowed intrinsic sucrose to express as a clean honeyed finish. Anaerobic Natural process transformed malic acid into jammy apple paste.

Sensory_Verdict: Damn the taste so nice the orange nectarine and finishing with that honey is terrific. Love this one. So far my favorite and the honey sweetness lingers around and taste changes once the temperature cools down.
Technical_Enrichment: Controlled Terroir Isolate: Brewed on Option-O Lagom P64 (64mm flats) and flatbed dripper, matching Asylum Entry #013/#014. Provides pure terroir delta between Colombia and Peru Geshas. Acaia Pearl confirmed precise 1:15.3 ratio execution at 92°C to maximize floral ester retention and stabilize malic acids.

Target_Notes: Fresh Apricot, Rooibos, Lemon Thyme, Toffee Apple
Sensory_Verdict: Opening: tartaric apricot + rooibos aspalathin. Mid: thymol terpene coat — lipid-binding, persistent to midway. Cooling: malic apple shift + caramelised sucrose. Clean transparent fade. No linalool/jasmine — distinct from Peru Geisha entries.
Technical_Enrichment: Triple-temp cascade (92→75→92°C) on CORE flat burr + Hario Alpha flat-bottom preserved heat-sensitive thymol terpenes from 2,100 MASL Loja terroir — highest-altitude Geisha in archive. Terpene-forward Ecuador profile clearly differentiated from linalool-forward Peru Geisha.
